facts.raw_span: A woman in her 60s presented with a 3-month history of pain, swelling, and erythema on her face
left breast carcinoma diagnosed eleven years earlier
treated with mastectomy, radiotherapy, and chemotherapy
left supraclavicular lymph nodes metastasis treated with surgical excision
pain on palpation
no fever or chills
Violaceous swelling with telangiectasia and necrosis on the forehead, eyelids, nose, and cheek, predominantly involving the left side of the face
Hyperkeratosis, epidermal atrophy, and dilated vessels in the dermis
nests of highly atypical cells
Epithelial cells in the dilated vessels were positive for CD31
atypical cells were strongly positive for GATA3
telangiectatic, swelling erythema mainly involving the left side of the forehead, eyelids, nose, and cheek

concepts.why: The patient has a history of breast carcinoma with metastasis, and the current symptoms and histopathological findings are consistent with cutaneous metastasis.
The presence of telangiectasia, dilated vessels, and atypical cells in the dermis, along with the patient's history of breast carcinoma, suggests the possibility of angiosarcoma.
The patient's symptoms of pain, swelling, and erythema on the face, along with the history of breast carcinoma, are consistent with inflammatory breast carcinoma.
The presence of telangiectasia and metastatic breast carcinoma cells in the dermis suggests a diagnosis of telangiectatic metastatic breast carcinoma.
The presence of atypical cells in dilated vessels, along with the expression of CD31 and GATA3, suggests an atypical vascular lesion.
The patient's symptoms of pain, swelling, and erythema on the face, along with the presence of atypical cells, suggest the possibility of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma.
The patient's symptoms of pain, swelling, and erythema on the face, along with the presence of necrosis, suggest the possibility of granulomatosis with polyangiitis.
The patient's symptoms of pain, swelling, and erythema on the face, along with the presence of telangiectasia, suggest the possibility of erythema elevatum diutinum.

rationales.F02: History of breast carcinoma increases the likelihood of cutaneous metastatic breast carcinoma.
rationales.F04: History of lymph node metastasis increases the likelihood of cutaneous metastatic breast carcinoma.
rationales.F07: Telangiectatic swelling and necrosis are characteristic of angiosarcoma and telangiectatic metastatic breast carcinoma.
rationales.F09: Presence of highly atypical cells in dilated vessels is characteristic of angiosarcoma and metastatic breast carcinoma.
rationales.F10: CD31 positivity in epithelial cells suggests vascular origin, consistent with angiosarcoma and metastatic breast carcinoma.
rationales.F11: GATA3 positivity in atypical cells suggests breast origin, consistent with metastatic breast carcinoma.
